suites.notes: Protocol: bounded blocking-I/O worker pool (submit/dequeue/complete/get/shutdown). Liveness checked via FairSpec temporal property; negative models gate worker-bound and shutdown-drain regressions. (Audit fix: binding was the dangling src/core/blocking_io_pool.cpp.)

Protocol: RequestArena/RequestSlot explicit-I/O accepted-request lifecycle (five-stage admission, Scheme-B enqueue/cancel arbitration, terminal-winner exactly-once, running-cancel intent verbatim law, reap-only publication gated on the acknowledged enqueue pin, generation advance before reuse, borrow-through-reap). Closes the former request-arena-lifecycle formal-debt gap with the smallest single-slot model (e13 FAULT-constant negatives NEG-RA-1..6, wrong-property controls, witnesses W1-W5; residual multi-slot ready-ring ORDER scope recorded in the coverage gap). Authority layering (PR #125 review P1): the two detail headers are the Layer-A leaf-safety authority the model proves; the two backend files bind the Layer-B EXTERNAL obligations only — WF(Enqueue) is the submit-path obligation (enqueue_after_commit) and WF(Reap) is the progress-loop obligation (poll/wait_one/reaper call sites of arena_.reap), neither guaranteed by the arena leaf, and every cfg sets CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE (no deadlock-freedom claim). RecordCanceledConfirmed is a BACKEND obligation: the leaf record_canceled checks only state/exactly-once (no provenance) and has NO production caller today — future backend obligation, exercised by tests and pinned adversarially by NEG-RA-6. NEG-RA-2's stale key is causal (committed and freed in an earlier generation racing the W4 reuse).

Protocol: rwlock writer-fair FIFO reconcile (unlock/cancel/expire head-prefix grant) plus timed admission (*_lock_until). Negative models: ReaderBypass (admission barging), NoReconcile (release drops grant-from-head, stranding a grantable head), WriterRevoke (MODEL-002 control: writer reconcile drops the activeReaders = 0 guard, revoking a live reader), and DeadlinePrecedence (MODEL-003 control: a due deadline wins over an admissible resource while the evidence latches stay TRUE, violating InvResourceFirstDeadline) — the latter two GENERATED from the positive model by scripts/formal/gen-rwlock-neg-writer-revoke.py and gen-rwlock-neg-deadline-precedence.py, whose --check freshness modes run inside verify-async-rwlock.sh BEFORE TLC (a stale committed negative fails the gate; the IF-form ghost is required because an unparenthesized x' = y \/ c parses as (x' = y) \/ c under TLA+ precedence — a language pitfall, not a TLC limitation). Reachability witnesses (MODEL-001 closure, non-vacuity): cancel/expire reader-prefix merge, cancel/expire writer-refused head stays blocked, and the writer-blocked contrast — each NoReach* is violated, proving the reconcile branches fire in the as-built model — plus the two MODEL-003 timed-admission halves (resource beats an already-due deadline; inline admission-expire when not admissible). Positive gate checks 13 invariants including ReaderRevocationFree (RW10) and InvResourceFirstDeadline (RW11, MODEL-003 closure at parity with E12Semaphore P7 / E12AsyncMutex M7).

Protocol: issue #161 combined rwlock-publication x idle-dance termination liveness (T22 multi-worker drain hang). Positive: repaired safety+liveness at the EXACT as-built constants (contribution-generation law; the three genuine invalidation sites bump — pop/mw_s1/route-publication — while the :958 recheck and :1065 reset-continue sites do NOT, matching C++ store(0); EraseIdleBumping bumps only when the erase actually erased a contribution), split-window safety on the all-bumps constants (the window costs only a transient park), two B4 self-guarded-site proofs (:958/:1065), M1/M2/M3 composition on the repaired base (documented in-scope closure — those hazard classes need a non-worker producer or unbounded busy owner; carried by e9 negatives at its abstraction). Negative: M4 as-built DrainStuckState + liveness CEX (an unlocked or route-publication erase orphans a not-last dancer's contribution; its stale 1-bit R4 flag lets the park commit absorb the eraser's not-last signal; both workers sleep with work complete), M5 grant-without-ticket, and the three genuine invalidation sites (:550 pop-erase, :582 mw_s1 erase, and the route-publication erase RECLASSIFIED genuine by the split-window model — the two unlocked sites are modeled as the split exchange/bump pairs the C++ performs). Reachability witness: E12SchedLivenessSplitWindow violates SplitWindowNeverArmed (the exchange(0)-before-bump window a park commit can observe); the repaired-constants safety gate on the same split constants proves the window costs only a transient park. SF on TryPop encodes own-inbox straight-line pop scheduling (steal-war closure); wake epoch is monotonic Nat.

coverage_gaps.why_no_model_yet: The single-slot load-bearing core is now modeled (suite request-arena, 2026-08-18 formal audit; smallest-model rule of AGENTS.md section 17). The residual gap is deliberately open: ready-ring FIFO ORDER across >=2 simultaneous backend_ready slots multiplies the state space for a property whose load-bearing content (per-slot order preservation between terminal winner and reap publication) is already covered by the single-slot model plus executable evidence. Modeling it requires a capacity-2 suite variant; do not read the current suite as multi-slot coverage.

coverage_gaps.not_covered_by_existing_suites: The request-arena suite covers the single-slot lifecycle core. NOT covered by any model: (a) ready-ring reap ORDER across two or more simultaneously backend_ready slots (ADR Decision 9 backend-known order); (b) multi-slot interference on the free list / accounting under concurrency; (c) the backend admission transaction around commit (Completion idle->binding->outstanding publication — Completion authority, AGENTS.md 4.3). These remain executable-evidence scope. Adjacent suites do not cover them: e7/e8 model runnable tickets/ownership, e9/e10 scheduler wake/wait-queue, e16 the runtime epoch.
